newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER UNITED FACTS AND FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER UNITED FACTS AND FIGURES.

text.p: Facts and figures relating to Saturday's Liverpool v Manchester United English premier league match at Anfield:

Manchester United: Formed 1878 as Newton Heath, changed name to Manchester United 1902. Major honours: European champions 1968; European Cup Winners' Cup winners: 1991. English League champions: 1908, 1911, 1952, 1956, 1957, 1965, 1967, 1993, 1994, 1996. F.A. Cup Winners: 1909, 1948, 1963, 1977, 1983, 1985, 1990, 1994, 1996. League Cup winners: 1992. Double winners: 1994, 1996
Record league goalscorer: Bobby Charlton 199 goals, 1956-73
Liverpool v Manchester United league record:
(Clubs had met in 1890s when United were still known as Newton Heath)
Manchester United 6 Liverpool 1, Old Trafford, May 5 1928
Note: Liverpool beat Newton Heath, the forerunners of Manchester United, 7-1 on October 12 1895.
December 17 1995: Liverpool 2 (Robbie Fowler 2) Manchester United 0. Attendance: 40,546

Other facts: Only nine players have ever been transferred directly between the two clubs in more than 100 years. The last was Phil Chisnall, a 21-year-old winger who moved from Manchester United to Liverpool 33 years ago.

United have won only one of their last nine league meetings at Anfield -- a run that immediately followed an eight-match run from April 1981 to December 1986 when they were unbeaten in eight league matches there.

When Manchester United won the F.A. Cup in 1948 they became the first, and so far only, team to play six teams from the top division on their way to victory at Wembley. Drawn at home against Liverpool in the third round, the match was switched to Everton's ground Goodison Park as Old Trafford was still out of use because of damage sustained in the Second World War. United won 3-0.
